snippet.title: Why Letting Your Dog Pull on Its Collar Backfires
snippet.description:
Vets at the University of Wisconsin measured eye pressure in 51 eyes of 26 dogs while the dogs pulled against a leash attached to a collar and to a harness. With the collar, the pressure inside the eyes rose significantly, on average by 7.4 mmHg; with the harness, the small rise of 2.3 mmHg was not significant. The authors advise a harness instead of a collar, especially for dogs with glaucoma, thin corneas or other eye problems. A comfy, well-fitted harness takes the strain off the neck.

Animated by Bit Cinema Team
Sound design by Bit Cinema Team

Source:
Pauli, A. M., Bentley, E., Diehl, K. A. & Miller, P. E. (2006). Effects of the application of neck pressure by a collar or harness on intraocular pressure in dogs. Journal of the American Animal Hospital Association 42(3), 207-211.
https://doi.org/10.5326/0420207

snippet.title: Cats can lose their TAIL
snippet.description: Cats' tails are part of their spine, with about twenty little bones in them. That's almost one out of every ten bones in their whole body. If a tail gets hurt, it usually hangs down and your cat can't lift it, so that's the sign to watch for.The good news is that lots of cats get their pee control back in a few weeks if the nerves were only stretched. And cats without a tail still walk and jump just fine, because their balance comes mostly from their inner ear. Has your cat ever hurt their tail?
